event.title: Fatal family accident and Vincent’s assumption of Adam’s identity
event.description: The original Adam Pleskot and his parents die when their car falls off a cliff during their trip to Great Orme; no one in the car survives. Vincent takes advantage of his resemblance to Adam, replaces Adam’s body and assumes his identity.

participant.role: protagonist; Vincent operating as Adam Pleskot after the identity takeover
original identity holder; fatal accident victim

inputs.description: Vincent’s arrival in 1972 makes him present to take advantage of the accident.
Vincent closely resembles the original Adam Pleskot.

outcomes.description: The original Adam and both parents are dead; there are no survivors of the car accident.
Vincent operates under Adam Pleskot’s identity.

event.title: Adam matches six LOTTO 6aus49 winning numbers
event.description: During his Frankfurt stay, Adam takes part in Germany’s LOTTO 6aus49 and uses foreknowledge to match all six winning numbers.

participant.role: protagonist; Vincent operating as Adam Pleskot after the identity takeover

inputs.description: Adam’s move to Frankfurt places him in Germany to enter the lottery.
Knowledge of the winning numbers from the original timeline.

outcomes.description: Adam holds a lottery entry matching six winning numbers; the prize is collected separately on 20 February.

event.title: Adam opens securities accounts and begins NYSE investing
event.description: Adam opens securities accounts at First National City Bank in New York and starts investing on the NYSE, using his knowledge of the original future in accordance with his financial strategy.

participant.role: protagonist; Vincent operating as Adam Pleskot after the identity takeover

inputs.description: Adam’s relocation to New York places him there to open securities accounts and begin investing.
The lottery proceeds of DM 800,000 (USD 248,000 equivalent) have been deposited in Adam’s First National City Bank account in New York and provide the starting capital for investment from March 1972.
Adam’s investment strategy uses secret foreknowledge, with contemporary evidence becoming more important as his actions change markets.

outcomes.description: Adam has opened securities accounts at First National City Bank and begun NYSE investment activity. Subsequent wealth growth is not treated as an immediate result of opening the accounts.

event.title: Investment-data office established
event.description: Starts an office with three workers, a PDP-11/40 and three terminals. Workers manually capture New York Times stock prices, sales, other statistics and company/market sentiment measures.

outcomes.description: Data supports analysis and prediction; algorithms serve as a cover for unusual investment success.

event.title: Joint DRI founding and funding
event.description: On 7 December 1974 Gary Kildall, Dorothy McEwen and Adam formalise and finance DRI, following the formation of Logix Tech, AION Labs and AION Software. Gary and Dorothy independently manage DRI’s engineering and operations; Adam contributes minority capital, strategy and OEM relationships to support CP/M-compatible personal computing. DRI retains CP/M ownership and independent licensing. Hardware abstraction and documented interfaces begin here, with optional ROM, memory and TUI services developed progressively.

inputs.description: Formation of Logix Tech, AION Labs and AION Software establishes Adam’s companies and the basis for the planned technology cooperation.

outcomes.description: DRI is established with agreed funding, independent founder management and CP/M ownership, providing an operating-system partner for the planned computers.

event.title: Three technology companies founded
event.description: On 23 November 1974 Adam establishes Logix Tech in San Jose, California, for computers and associated software; AION Labs in Cambridge, England, for semiconductors; and AION Software in Copenhagen, Denmark, for business applications and compilers. He has prepared a recruitment shortlist for a CEO, CFO and CTO at each company and begins approaching candidates for these nine leadership roles.

inputs.description: Adam’s established stock-market investment activity provides the funding basis for company formation.
Adam brings a prepared leadership shortlist and an understanding of future technology and market needs.

outcomes.description: The three companies exist before the DRI founding agreement of 7 December 1974.
Recruitment begins for separate CEO, CFO and CTO positions in San Jose, Cambridge and Copenhagen; individual appointments remain unspecified.

event.title: Secret future-equipped facility established
event.description: Brings CAD and laser-lithography equipment from the 2020s and establishes a facility separate from the three companies.

outcomes.description: Future chip-design tools supplement a publicly conservative semiconductor operation.

event.title: Logix and DRI agree CP/M development for Aurelia
event.description: Building on the established DRI partnership, Logix and DRI agree a new CP/M version for Aurelia, fully owned by DRI and available to other vendors. Its development scope includes a text-mode TUI, Plug and Execute smart devices/cards over FlexiBUS, XIP cartridges and names for CP/M User Numbers.

inputs.description: The earlier DRI founding and funding milestone establishes the independent operating-system partner and relationship on which this CP/M collaboration is based.

outcomes.description: The agreed product is a new CP/M version for Logix Aurelia, fully owned by DRI and available for non-exclusive licensing to other vendors. Its scope includes XIP cartridges and named CP/M user areas; implementation and qualification follow this agreement.
The agreement establishes integration of the Logix TUI standard into the CP/M development scope: a consistent pseudo-window user interface in text mode for participating applications.

The agreement establishes CP/M integration work for FlexiBUS smart devices and expansion cards using Plug and Execute. This outcome covers agreed software support, not invention or completed manufacture of the underlying bus.

event.title: BPI accepts investment and C/TUI redevelopment agreement
event.description: BPI Systems accepts Adam’s $150,000 investment in exchange for a 33% fully diluted interest. The agreement obliges AION Software to provide knowledge and resources to refactor BPI’s existing code into C with a competitive text-mode TUI. Further investment supports ports to future systems and platforms, after which BPI has the right to buy back Adam’s shares.

inputs.description: BPI contributes its existing application code and domain knowledge; AION contributes engineering expertise and resources for C and TUI redevelopment. This refers to pre-existing BPI source material, not a completed Aurelia C/TUI edition.

outcomes.description: BPI accepts the $150,000 subscription for Adam’s 33% fully diluted interest and the accompanying AION C/TUI redevelopment obligations. The deal also provides for further platform-porting investment and BPI’s subsequent right to buy back Adam’s shares.

event.title: BPI development and distribution cooperation
event.description: BPI and Adam implement operational cooperation under the consolidated BPI agreement: independent BPI management, brand, application ownership, licences and specialist support; AION engineering assistance and Logix distribution/training. This cooperation implements the accepted $150,000 investment agreement for Adam’s 33% fully diluted interest, including AION’s C/TUI redevelopment work and future-platform cooperation. Date selected for the alternative scenario. The cooperation also provides for later launch qualification, BPI-authorised Academy training and direct sales, with BPI retaining its software, independent licensing and specialist support.

inputs.description: BPI's accepted 15 February investment and C/TUI redevelopment agreement establishes the obligations implemented by this operational cooperation.

outcomes.description: The partners establish arrangements for qualifying independently licensed BPI applications and supporting their launch, dealer preparation and BPI-authorised Logix Computer Academy courses. BPI retains application ownership, licences and specialist support.

The cooperation supports a later programme of BPI-authorised courses and direct sales starting on 17 July 1978, after the NCC premiere. This start is separate from the Academy's March establishment and June 5 five-city public announcement.

event.title: Gordon Letwin recruited
event.description: Recruits Gordon Letwin from his then-current employer.

outcomes.description: Letwin never joins Microsoft in this scenario.

event.title: Tim Paterson recruited
event.description: Recruits Tim Paterson.

outcomes.description: Paterson does not develop QDOS and is unavailable to Microsoft.

event.title: OEM printer-mechanism agreement
event.description: Agree OEM purchasing/manufacturing arrangements for bare MP-40 mechanisms to receive FlexiBUS controllers.

outcomes.description: Agree OEM purchasing/manufacturing arrangements for the bare MP-40 printer mechanism to receive FlexiBUS controllers in Logix printer integration. This records procurement scope, not completed printer delivery.

event.title: AIONix preliminary architecture and portability work
event.description: Begin funded exploratory architecture, C portability and future ERA operating-system work before Aurelia launch. Preserve CP/M maintenance and the Aurelia release team. The September 12 agreement later formalises ownership, staffing and funding; preliminary work does not move product availability.

outcomes.description: Begin exploratory architecture, C portability and ERA operating-system work on the AIONix implementation; this is the start of development, not delivery of a customer software offering.

event.title: ComputerLand retail agreement
event.description: Arrange computer sales through ComputerLand as the planned primary channel.

event.title: BPI business and accountant pilot programme
event.description: Target 10–15 pilot businesses and several accounting practices; reconcile results against existing records. Validate representative data volumes, disk/RAM budgets, posting, corrections, backup/restore and supported payroll jurisdictions before launch claims. Date selected for the alternative scenario.

inputs.description: The candidate CP/M implementation supplies the application under test; representative business records and resource budgets define the pilot, without presuming every jurisdiction or configuration is accepted.

outcomes.description: Reconcile pilot results and test posting, corrections, backup/restore, resource limits and supported payroll jurisdictions before making launch claims. This qualification activity does not guarantee that every pilot or configuration passes.

event.title: Logix Computer Academy established
event.description: Establishes the Academy company and prepares rented facilities for an initial five-city US programme; publicly presented at the June 5 Aurelia premiere. City names and first course dates remain unspecified; capacity expands with demand.

outcomes.description: Establish the Logix Computer Academy company and prepare rented facilities for the initial five-city programme; city names and first course dates remain unspecified.

event.title: Aurelia newspaper teaser campaign begins
event.description: Newspaper and business-press teasers introduce Aurelia and the personal-assistant promise; coming this spring, followed by June 5 launch date; brochure and invitation requests.

event.title: Aurelia cinematic advertising campaign
event.description: Cinematic TV commercial and explanatory print advertisements; prioritise markets with demonstration, support and Academy coverage. Proposed Michael Douglas therapy-session reveal; casting remains subject to agreement. No AI or unhealthy-dependency claim.

event.title: Aurelia platform launches
event.description: Aurelia premieres on 5 June 1978 with startup, common editing, safe peripheral attachment, Business Tools and the eight-minute Abacus demonstration. DRI, MPI and BPI introduce their partnerships; Academy and dealer configurations follow. BPI’s dedicated application launch session takes place the following day at NCC. Questions follow the premiere presentation.

inputs.description: The established Academy company and prepared facilities provide the organisation for the training presentation; first course dates remain unspecified.

outcomes.description: Platform includes AION software, peripherals, support, developer programs and Academy training.

Academy Fundamentals offers two days of hands-on learning before purchase; 50% tuition credit valid six months toward one Aurelia, redeemable at Academy or participating dealers reimbursed by Logix. Orders accepted at training; no purchase obligation. Locations, tuition and first class dates must be published once selected.

event.title: Independent BPI Systems launches Aurelia applications
event.description: On 6 June 1978, the day after the Aurelia premiere, BPI presents its separately licensed five-module application family in a dedicated NCC session. The demonstration covers source records and summary export for Abacus. The head of BPI explains independent management, ownership and support and cooperation with Adam, AION and Logix. No personal identity for the head is specified.

inputs.description: The five-module application build and documented summary-export workflow supply the independently licensed BPI demonstration.

outcomes.description: Dealer configurations combine separately identified suppliers; BPI is not a Logix division. A documented BPI-to-Abacus summary export supports planning without modifying accounting records.

event.title: SMC second-source and technology-transfer agreement
event.description: Start independent second-source manufacturing and sales cooperation after Aurelia’s premiere. AION transfers working reference silicon, SMC-compatible ready-to-use masks, process know-how and production-test specifications; SMC supplies process/mask requirements and performs its own wafer fabrication. Logix supplies reference boards, system tests and initial purchase commitments.

outcomes.description: Agree independent second-source fabrication and technology-transfer work for the FlexiBUS host/device controllers, Aurelia video controller and 4116-equivalent DRAM. Reference silicon, masks, process know-how and production tests define the transfer scope; availability still requires SMC qualification.

event.title: Apple coordinates business-software recruitment
event.description: Respond to Aurelia with a coordinated search for accounting, spreadsheet and database partners, engineering access and demonstration systems. Disk II development already predates Aurelia; this is a change in software/commercial priority, not the invention of disk support.

outcomes.description: Establish the response described in Apple coordinates business-software recruitment.

event.title: BPI training, direct sales and qualified dealer programme begin
event.description: On 17 July 1978, Academy begins BPI-authorised practical courses and direct distribution alongside BPI dealer qualification, accountant demonstration access, permission-based case studies and defined paid setup assistance. Each initial Academy centre has access to a BPI specialist. Dealers handle first-line installation enquiries, BPI handles software defects and specialist support, and Logix supports hardware. Tuition, setup services and software licences remain separate.

participant.role: authorised training and direct distribution provider

inputs.description: The BPI application launch establishes the product offering for subsequent authorised training, direct distribution and dealer demonstrations.
Separately licensed BPI applications are the subject of the authorised courses, direct distribution and dealer demonstrations. They remain BPI offerings rather than newly created Academy software.

outcomes.description: Authorised BPI training, direct sales and the qualified dealer programme are operating with defined support responsibilities and access to BPI specialists.

event.title: AIONix development programme and ownership formalised
event.description: Formalise the AIONix programme begun in February 1978: joint ERA development in assembler and C, funded by AION. Existing ownership, equity and future porting-right terms remain.

inputs.description: The AIONix department's February move to Logix offices near DRI supplies the working arrangement for the programme formalised in September.

outcomes.description: Formalise ownership, staffing and funding for the AIONix implementation under the governing agreement. The decision does not itself deliver released software.

event.title: Apple business-dealer demonstration programme
event.description: Prepare complete-system quotations, repeatable business-workflow demonstrations and introductory customer lessons. Initial implementation is selective, not an instantly nationwide training network.

outcomes.description: Establish the response described in Apple business-dealer demonstration programme.

event.title: Apple seeks business-software partners
event.description: Expand the July business-software initiative into partner negotiations for disk-based accounting, spreadsheets and databases; seek independent software alternatives to AION.

event.title: Adam opens confidential Model II cooperation talks
event.description: After Aurelia launch and growing dealer sales, Adam demonstrates Abacus and proposes an official Model II CP/M configuration plus FlexiBUS in return for an AION-funded Abacus adaptation. Talks occur during the scenario early-design window; no historical design-freeze date is asserted. Confidential talks have no immediate mass-market demand effect.

inputs.description: The existing Aurelia Abacus implementation provides the application demonstrated in the cooperation talks; the Model II port is not yet the supplied implementation.
The scenario’s Model II design work supplies the prospective native-hardware target for negotiation. This does not assert that the later retail configuration is already released.

outcomes.description: Establish the response described in Adam opens confidential Model II cooperation talks.
Propose a supported Model II CP/M configuration, an AION-funded Abacus adaptation and a qualified FlexiBUS option. These are negotiation targets, not completed deliverables.

event.title: External CP/M extension qualification begins
event.description: Begin external OEM implementations, developer documentation and qualification of portable TUI/FlexiBUS extensions, executing the portability policy established at DRI founding.

inputs.description: The CP/M collaboration establishes DRI ownership and non-exclusive reuse rights for the operating-system enhancements. This is the direct agreement basis; the earlier founding event is not repeated as a transitive prerequisite.
Portable implementations must preserve the documented text-interface contract while qualifying host-specific integrations.

outcomes.description: Work begins on host-specific implementations, developer documentation and qualification of the portable extensions. This records the start of implementation work, not a completed portable release.

event.title: Tandy, Logix, DRI and AION sign Model II cooperation agreement
event.description: Tandy commits to officially selling/supporting CP/M and a qualified FlexiBUS option for Model II, supplies engineering access and distributes Abacus. DRI supplies CP/M and required platform services. Logix supplies interface documentation, reference engineering and initial chips. AION funds the port, corrects incompatibilities, qualifies and maintains the Model II edition. Tandy keeps native video, keyboard, disk architecture, legacy ports, branding, sales and first-line support. No Logix video or CP/M-6502 commitment.

inputs.description: The cooperation talks establish the proposed porting and interface scope negotiated into this agreement.

outcomes.description: Establish the response described in Tandy, Logix, DRI and AION sign Model II cooperation agreement.

Commit the parties to supported CP/M, a Model II Abacus port and a qualified internal FlexiBUS option while retaining Tandy’s native hardware and customer support. Implementation and qualification follow the agreement.

event.title: Model II compatibility design baseline agreed
event.description: Reserve an internal option-board slot and interface/power budget before the scenario design baseline is closed. Freeze CP/M BIOS responsibilities, native display/keyboard adapter and the FlexiBUS connector plan. This review is an invented alternate-history engineering milestone, not a claim about the real Model II freeze date.

inputs.description: The signed cooperation agreement supplies the responsibilities and interface scope to freeze in the design review.
The Model II native bus, slot, power, display, keyboard and storage architecture constrain the compatibility design.

outcomes.description: Establish the response described in Model II compatibility design baseline agreed.
Set the CP/M BIOS responsibilities, native interface adaptation and qualified internal FlexiBUS connector plan. This is a design baseline, not a completed release.

event.title: Stepper programme approved and equipment ordered
event.description: AION approves the existing January 1979 stepper programme and orders a compatible pair of GCA reduction steppers with reticle metrology, spares, supplier training and service support. Procurement begins the development programme; installation, tool matching and product qualification remain separate gates.

inputs.description: A stable existing production route and its measured limitations support the next lithography investment.

outcomes.description: Funded lithography procurement and supplier support enable development of the 2.75 µm route.

event.title: Apple partners with Peachtree
event.description: Develop an Apple II accounting offering with Peachtree while separately pursuing spreadsheet and database suppliers. Peachtree is not treated as a substitute for Abacus by itself. Start a partnership for an Apple II business offering.

inputs.description: The partnership targets accounting software and setup/support appropriate to Apple II, rather than a replacement Logix computer platform.

outcomes.description: In the scenario, VisiCalc is less advanced in spreadsheet size and available features.

event.title: Logix and Apple agree limited technical cooperation
event.description: Requests documentation, test machines and compatibility assistance for native Apple II FlexiBUS, disk interoperability and Logix video products. Agrees to limited technical cooperation and compatibility assistance.

inputs.description: Native expansion and disk/video interoperability must target the existing Apple II host. Access to documentation and test machines is sought through this cooperation, not presumed already delivered.

outcomes.description: Apple accepts Logix-funded native expansion as a way to increase installed Apple II utility, with separate branding/support and no requirement to adopt the full Logix platform; its own peripheral strategy continues.
The accepted cooperation covers native Apple II expansion, disk interoperability and Logix video products. It establishes compatibility assistance, not completion or sale of the hardware.

event.title: Model II CP/M and Abacus prototype review
event.description: Review prototype CP/M boot, Tandy disk/printer BIOS, native TUI adapter and Abacus document interchange. Resolve ROM/banking assumptions and measure available RAM on the 64 KB target. FlexiBUS prototype is specific to the Tandy bus, not a plug-in S-100 card.

inputs.description: The agreed compatibility baseline provides the interface and responsibility constraints against which prototypes are reviewed.
Prototype CP/M and Abacus builds and the Model II-specific FlexiBUS prototype supply the work under review. Their current prototype state does not establish customer availability.

outcomes.description: Establish the response described in Model II CP/M and Abacus prototype review.
Review boot, native UI, disk/printer BIOS and document interchange, resolving banking assumptions and measuring available RAM on the 64 KB Model II target. No universal pass or shipment is implied.

event.title: Independent OEM and peripheral engineering briefings
event.description: Begin confidential briefings and engineering-kit evaluations. Prioritise North Star and Vector Graphic as prospects; approach Cromemco, Altos, Intertec and Heath selectively. Invitations are not signed agreements or qualified products. This day is a selected scenario milestone.

event.title: Apple promotes complete business configurations
event.description: Participating dealers promote Apple II/Disk II business configurations, demonstrations and introductory lessons; Apple pursues spreadsheet distribution/development support separately from Peachtree accounting. No completed VisiCalc release or finished March 1980 Apple–Peachtree package is pulled into spring 1979.

inputs.description: The dealer-demonstration programme supplies repeatable workflows and introductory lessons for these participating-dealer promotions.
The demonstrations use Apple II-based business configurations; a finished Apple–Peachtree package is not a prerequisite for these earlier promotions.

outcomes.description: Establish the response described in Apple promotes complete business configurations.

event.title: Portable CP/M extensions released
event.description: Release documented, optional CP/M Platform Extensions for non-Logix manufacturers: TUI, capability discovery and FlexiBUS adapters. Ordinary CP/M remains usable without these facilities; hardware and application resource requirements still apply.

inputs.description: The portable implementation and qualification programme supplies the documented host-specific extensions released here.

outcomes.description: The CP/M ecosystem retains an opportunity to expand.

Release the documented optional CP/M Platform Extensions for non-Logix manufacturers, with TUI, capability discovery and FlexiBUS adapters. Existing host requirements remain; this is not delivery of an Aurelia ROM cartridge.

event.title: Publish independent compatibility programmes
event.description: Alongside the existing DRI portable-extension release, publish separate CP/M application, FlexiBUS peripheral and optional Logix display compatibility profiles, reference-driver and test access, non-exclusive implementation principles and support-roadmap requirements. Exact fees and support duration remain to be settled. This day is a selected scenario milestone.

event.title: Pre-NCC cross-vendor qualification workshop
event.description: Invite computer, software and peripheral suppliers to test named configurations and document failures before public demonstrations. Supplier attendance and passing results must be verified; no announcement of an unsigned OEM. This day is a selected scenario milestone.

event.title: Model II announced with planned CP/M, FlexiBUS and Abacus offering
event.description: Publicly announce Model II and the planned officially supported CP/M/Abacus configuration and FlexiBUS option. Preserve the historical late-May announcement window, June NCC demonstrations and October US delivery window. Announcements and orders are not completed computer or Abacus sales.

inputs.description: The prototype review provides the engineering basis for bounded planned-compatibility claims; an announcement or order is not a completed sale.

outcomes.description: Establish the response described in Model II announced with planned CP/M, FlexiBUS and Abacus offering.

event.title: Microsoft BASIC presented
event.description: Microsoft releases Microsoft BASIC for Aurelia at NCC 1979 as licensed third-party software.

inputs.description: The licensed Aurelia CP/M BASIC implementation is the software released and demonstrated by Microsoft.

event.title: Model II CP/M, FlexiBUS and Abacus demonstrated at NCC
event.description: Demonstrate Abacus using the native Model II display/keyboard, a CP/M disk build and qualified prototype FlexiBUS peripherals. Distinguish demonstrations from customer releases; announce an autumn supported 64 KB configuration. No Logix video subsystem is required.

inputs.description: The NCC demonstration uses the native Model II host, a CP/M disk build, Abacus implementation and qualified prototype FlexiBUS peripherals. Demonstration readiness is distinct from the autumn customer release.

outcomes.description: Establish the response described in Model II CP/M, FlexiBUS and Abacus demonstrated at NCC.

event.title: NCC 1979 presentation and Apple II/S-100 expansion launch
event.description: On 4 June 1979, Logix holds its NCC open-architecture and migration presentation and launches the Apple II Expansion Card, FlexiDisk II, S-100 FlexiBUS Interface, Apple II Video Card and S-100 Video Card. An Apple representative participates in the native Apple demonstration. The cards initially use AION chips and ship with the applicable native Apple drivers/examples or supported S-100 CP/M adapters. Apple participates in the native Apple demonstration without endorsing S-100 systems.

inputs.description: The Apple technical cooperation agreement provides the documentation, test machines and compatibility assistance used for the native Apple expansion products.
The portable DRI extension release provides documented software services used in supported compatibility demonstrations and S-100 CP/M integration.

outcomes.description: The open-architecture and migration programme is presented to NCC participants; product availability and development plans remain distinguished.
The five Apple II and S-100 expansion products have a recorded launch, with initial AION chip supply and host-appropriate drivers and adapters.

event.title: Detailed CP/M-80 compatibility module development begins
event.description: Begin confidential implementation work following the public June 4 migration commitment and preliminary feasibility work. Public language remains a planned optional Z80 coprocessor for qualified legacy applications; implementation details and future-platform specifications remain undisclosed until NCC 1980. This is the start of detailed implementation on 4 September 1979, not a shipment.

event.title: Confidential next-generation software and tool preparation
event.description: Prepare future system software internally; publish no names or architectural details before NCC 1980. Prepare application migration and future C tools internally. Public 1979 clinics use the established C environment and documented interfaces only; no future-target binaries, compiler output or SDK are distributed.

event.title: IBM investigates the personal-computer market
event.description: Confidentially benchmark Aurelia/Abacus business workflows, Tandy distribution and Apple software partnerships; examine price, training, service and independent OS suppliers. No public IBM product announcement or immediate buyer-deferral effect is assumed.

event.title: Compatibility roadshows and developer migration clinics
event.description: Run dealer demonstrations, joint trade-press activity and developer clinics. Teach documented APIs, file interchange, C portability boundaries and device-class drivers. Publish a directory distinguishing shipping, qualified and prototype configurations. This day is a selected scenario milestone.

event.title: Stepper installation and lithography acceptance
event.description: Selected alternative-history milestone; qualify measured process, retention/speed, tool matching and cost before release. Existing processors retain their current process. See memory_manufacturing.json.

inputs.description: The procurement order provides the equipment and installation support.

outcomes.description: Installation and optical acceptance measurements enable process-development lots; matched-pair volume capacity and recipe releases remain separate gates.

event.title: Apple reviews successor-product compatibility requirements
event.description: Competitive review increases priority for protecting existing software, peripherals and customer data in successor plans. This is a requirements decision, not a guaranteed technical fix or early Lisa/GUI shipment. Apple keeps its independent hardware roadmap.

outcomes.description: Establish the response described in Apple reviews successor-product compatibility requirements.

event.title: SMC begins licensed chip sales
event.description: Initial qualified SMC-manufactured chips become commercially available in the alternate timeline. This begins staged availability, not guaranteed release of every chip or mature yields; video RAM retains a separate qualification gate. SMC performs wafer fabrication rather than merely packaging AION dies.

inputs.description: The second-source agreement enables SMC fabrication, qualification and staged independent sales.

outcomes.description: AION remains the launch supplier for June 1979 cards. Qualified SMC parts become independently purchasable alternatives; no automatic procurement switch, price reduction or high-volume yield is asserted. The referenced chips identify the cooperation scope, not simultaneous release of every part; video RAM retains its separate qualification gate.

event.title: Supported Model II CP/M and Abacus configuration released
event.description: Scenario customer release within the historical October US shipping window: supported 64 KB CP/M configuration, Model II Abacus and the separately supported FlexiBUS option. Release follows disk, printing, save/reopen, native UI and interface qualification; publish resource limits. October 15 is a scenario-selected day. OEM economics and Tandy system prices are not inferred from Aurelia retail prices.

inputs.description: Customer release requires disk, printing, save/reopen, native UI and interface qualification with published resource limits. Earlier NCC demonstrations alone do not establish acceptance.

outcomes.description: Establish the response described in Supported Model II CP/M and Abacus configuration released.

event.title: Promote verified ecosystem deliveries
event.description: Promote the separately recorded Tandy customer release and only individually qualified SMC or peripheral products. Update directory evidence; do not imply all licensed chips, every peripheral class or new independent OEM systems are shipping. This day is a selected scenario milestone.

event.title: First complete 2.75 µm pilot lots
event.description: Selected alternative-history milestone; qualify measured process, retention/speed, tool matching and cost before release. Existing processors retain their current process. See memory_manufacturing.json.

outcomes.description: First complete 2.75 µm pilot lots

event.title: Aurelia+, Pulse, Abacus 2.0 and manufacturer compatibility kit arrive
event.description: Launches Aurelia+. Presents Pulse and Abacus 2.0. Makes corresponding training available. Launch the Aurelia Software Compatibility Kit with published contracts, reference runtime adapters, diagnostics and application acceptance tests. Manufacturers may independently implement the released environment; optional paid support and certification use standard terms. Application redistribution remains separately licensed. Shift new hardware development and promotion to Aurelia+ while enabling independent Aurelia-class clones. Continue installed-base support and compatible software; do not impose an immediate Aurelia withdrawal. FlexiBUS and Logix video adoption remain separate choices. Future architecture details remain undisclosed until NCC 1980. Present the 45-minute COMDEX campaign plus questions: More room to work. More freedom to choose. Run identical live calculated shaded-cube and Abacus workloads on Aurelia and Aurelia+ under equivalent conditions; show measured results without an unverified speed multiplier. See comdex_1979_campaign.json. Demonstrate Abacus 2.0 charts and spreadsheet-linked layouts using precalculated fictitious employee values, then preview and print a complete payslip batch. The head of independent BPI follows Abacus with the source payroll and reconciled file-exchange workflow, and joins the partner segment. Abacus 2.0 also serves existing Aurelia owners.

participant.role: independent partner; head of BPI presents

inputs.description: The later BPI partner presentation supplies source payroll and reconciled file-exchange data for the Abacus demonstration; this is a repeat promotion and workflow dependency, not BPI’s original launch.

event.title: IBM starts its personal-computer project
event.description: Authorise a PC project because independent suppliers, including Logix, Tandy and Apple, are establishing business applications, interfaces and retail/service channels outside IBM. Do not assume a Logix–Apple duopoly. Initially expect external software to shorten development.

outcomes.description: DRI remains an independent licensor but its existing funded development and CP/M-80 commitments leave no committed x86 OS on IBM’s required schedule. Paterson’s recruitment removes the historical SCP 86-DOS route; Letwin’s absence reduces Microsoft staffing options. Alternatives remain possible. Supplier selection, substitute OS development and application qualification become the critical path toward early 1982, rather than technical impossibility.

event.title: Review end-1979 ecosystem adoption targets
event.description: Target Tandy shipping, one additional named OEM selling a supported CP/M-extension/FlexiBUS option, another OEM in qualification, dealer/integrator configurations and third-party devices in several categories. These are adoption targets, not recorded achievements or contracted orders. This day is a selected scenario milestone.

event.title: Customer evidence and compatibility programme review
event.description: Publish verified customer examples, compatibility results and partner configurations. Target three to five non-Logix manufacturers with supported configurations by NCC 1980, counting Tandy once and excluding duplicate dealer builds. Do not disclose the new processor architecture early. This day is a selected scenario milestone.

event.title: IBM software sourcing review exposes schedule gap
event.description: CP/M-86 does not exist. DRI prioritises CP/M-80/TUI, AIONix and PRO. Adam owns 30% of independent DRI and Logix competes with IBM, making schedule and strategic dependence concerns substantial. outcomes.description: Establish the response described in IBM software sourcing review exposes schedule gap.

event.title: Apple–Peachtree small-business package starts
event.description: Start a package with simplified setup, Apple II-oriented interface, documentation and support.

The package must operate on the Apple II host, with its platform-specific setup, interface and support requirements.

event.title: Artemis platform launches commercially
event.description: Launch Artemis with AIONix, peripherals, expansions, developer tooling and support. Introduces Artemis training. At NCC 1980 reveal the processor architecture and word size withheld in the NCC 1979 public campaign. The separately sold Z80 compatibility module is an optional qualified legacy path; native applications require an appropriate target build. Released Artemis application binaries using documented, supported ERA/AIONix interfaces retain a supported execution path on subsequent Logix professional platforms through 2000: native execution, a maintained compatibility runtime, or emulation. Source portability is a separate commitment, not a substitute for the binary execution path. Demonstrate familiar multitasking, separate ERA/Z80 C builds and qualified legacy-card execution; compare verified vector calculations on Aurelia+, PDP-11/34 and Artemis before revealing the 32-bit RISC ERA 1 architecture. Publish only measured performance. The head of independent BPI Systems presents after Abacus and joins the partner section; BPI retains separate branding, licences, support and receipts. Ship Artemis 128 with a replaceable 16 KiB video card and Mono II or Color II; ship Artemis 256 with 32 AION 64 Kbit system RAM chips, a 32 KiB video card and Mono Pro or Color II. Both cards include 1 KiB exclusive sprite SRAM. Only the professional card and Mono Pro enable 640×400 modes; Color II keeps legacy timings. High-resolution demonstrations and paid follow-up campaign are separately budgeted; production qualification remains required. Logix introduced an Artemis 128 KiB office configuration with two floppy drives, a Color Monitor II, keyboard, AIONix, Business Tools and one year of support. A second configuration added a 5 MB disk subsystem. Customers could add Abacus 3 from November 1980 and networking from May 1981.

inputs.description: Completion of the AIONix development phase on 20 February 1980 provides the operating-system work for subsequent integration and the Artemis commercial launch.

outcomes.description: Launch campaign and dated follow-up activities are specified in ncc_1980_campaign.json and NCC_1980_CAMPAIGN.md. Compatibility through 2000 is a commitment with eligibility and maintenance obligations, not evidence of future fulfilment.

event.title: Artemis Academy offering and regional institutional sales offices established
event.description: On 17 July 1980, Logix expands the Academy offering to Artemis-line products and combines Academy offices with regional sales offices prepared to sell computers directly to institutional clients. Sales staff may negotiate discounts for large contracts; no fixed discount rate or threshold is specified. Dealer demonstrations, customer workflow trials, press briefings, Academy transition classes and developer migration clinics support the rollout, with an issue and qualification register.

event.title: AIONix department relocates near DRI
event.description: On 24 February 1978, the AIONix department moves from Copenhagen to Logix offices near DRI headquarters.

inputs.description: The AIONix exploratory architecture and portability work begun on 1 February provides the programme context for relocating its department closer to DRI.

outcomes.description: The AIONix department is based at Logix offices near DRI headquarters to support the continuing development programme.

event.title: AION appoints its Cambridge manufacturing team
event.description: AION appoints a fab director, silicon-gate NMOS integration lead, lithography lead, facilities lead and test/reliability lead with production-ramp experience. Recruitment draws on established British, European and US semiconductor operations; individual names and former employers are unspecified. Supplier engineers train the new staff.

outcomes.description: The appointed team takes responsibility for defining and qualifying the Cambridge process and its controls.

event.description: The team accepts the installed line and repeatable test-structure operation. Pilot acceptance establishes engineering capability, not commercial product release.

event.description: Independent lots meet the selected ROM and 1 Kbit SRAM contracts. AION releases qualified order-specific ROMs and the initial SRAM grade for customer supply; the 4 Kbit extension and second-source licences require separate acceptance.

event.title: AION recruits DRAM process and test specialists

event.title: AION 16 Kbit DRAM production qualified
event.description: Independent lots of the AION 4116-equivalent meet released retention, refresh, timing, supply, package and reliability limits. The release supports manufacturing and inventory preparation for June 1978; no numeric yield is asserted.

event.description: AION appoints a yield manager, failure-analysis engineer, process-control engineers and maintenance specialists with authority to hold suspect lots and reject uncontrolled recipe changes.

event.title: AION releases its initial 3 µm 64 Kbit DRAM
event.description: Multiple independent lots meet the launch contract for retention, refresh, timing, rails, package and reliability. Release supports inventory for December 1979 Aurelia+ and reuse in Artemis; later control and repair revisions confer no early yield benefit.

event.title: ERAv1 design-to-fab baseline accepted
event.description: AION and Artemis engineering accept the initial 3 µm CPU design rules, mask revision, package and supply contract, representative logic structures and functional-test plan for pilot fabrication.

inputs.description: The demonstrated process windows constrain the CPU design and fabrication baseline.

outcomes.description: An agreed processor design-to-fab contract and test plan support CPU pilot manufacture.

event.title: ERAv1 manufacturing pilot silicon characterised
event.description: AION fabricates the initial CPU pilot revision and characterises function, timing, power and package behaviour. Engineering success does not authorise volume production or an 8 MHz grade.

event.title: ERAv1 6 MHz manufacturing route released for launch
event.description: Independent lots meet the released 6 MHz CPU specification, production-test coverage and package reliability requirements. Qualified launch stock and capacity are available for the May Artemis launch. The 8 MHz variant remains subject to separate silicon and grade qualification.

inputs.description: CPU pilot corrections are verified through independent qualification lots.

outcomes.description: The launch CPU recipe, test vectors, package contract and production controls are released.
